note: Taught: the President is elected by an electoral college of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies (Article 54).
Taught: a Money Bill cannot be introduced in Parliament without the recommendation (consent) of the President (Article 117(1)).
Taught: the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is the Vice-President of India, ex officio (Articles 64 and 89(1)).

Taught: the President causes the Finance Commission's recommendations (Article 281), the CAG's reports (Article 151) and the National Commission for Scheduled Castes' reports (Article 338) to be laid before Parliament; the Public Accounts Committee's report is presented by the Committee itself.
Taught: the impeachment of the President can be initiated in either House of Parliament (Article 61).
Taught: the power to grant pardons is enjoyed by the President (Article 72) and by the Governor of a State (Article 161).
Taught: a Money Bill cannot be introduced in Parliament without the recommendation (consent) of the President (Article 117(1)).
Taught: the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is the Vice-President of India (Articles 64 and 89(1)).
Taught: the President can take over the administration of a State (President's Rule) under Article 356.
Taught: the Vice-President is elected by an electoral college consisting of the members of both Houses of Parliament (Article 66); members of State legislatures do not vote.
Taught: the 44th Amendment (1978, w.e.f. 20-6-1979) made the written decision of the Union Cabinet mandatory before the President can proclaim a national emergency (Article 352(3)).
Taught: the President can declare a national emergency, a constitutional emergency (President's Rule) and a financial emergency (Articles 352, 356, 360).
Taught: before the expiry of his term the President can be removed from office only by impeachment by Parliament (Articles 56 and 61).
Taught: the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is the Vice-President (Articles 64 and 89(1)).
Taught: the Governor of a State is appointed by the President (Article 155).
Taught: the Attorney-General for India is appointed by the President (Article 76(1)).
Taught: the power to declare an Emergency is the President's (Articles 352, 356, 360).
Taught: President's Rule in a State is promulgated under Article 356.
Not taught: the chapter teaches that Vice-President B. D. Jatti acted as President on the death of Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed, but not that Zakir Hussain was the first President to die while in office.
Not taught: 'first citizen' is a conventional description of the President; it appears in neither the Constitution text nor NCERT Chapter 4 as used here.

Not taught: the chapter teaches that the President is eligible for re-election (Article 57) and that Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the first President, but not that he was the only President elected for a second time.
Not taught: the 'His Superfluous Highness' nickname for the Vice-President appears in neither the Constitution text nor NCERT Chapter 4 as used here.
Not taught here: the chapter teaches the President's appointment of Supreme Court judges (Article 124); the appointment of the Chief Justice of a High Court (Article 217) belongs to POL-12.
Not taught here: the Inter-State Council (Article 263) belongs to POL-15.
Not taught here: the Election Commission (Article 324) belongs to POL-17.
Not taught here: the power to increase the number of Supreme Court judges is Parliament's and belongs to POL-11.
Not taught: the chapter does not cover Pranab Mukherjee's ministerial career before becoming President.
